title: Lost Highway
events_chronological: Saxophonist Fred Madison suspects his wife Renee of an affair and cannot reach her in bed or anywhere else.
Videotapes start appearing on the doorstep, showing first the outside of the house, then the inside, then the couple asleep.
At a party Fred meets a pale Mystery Man who tells him he is inside Fred's house at that moment and hands him a phone that proves it.
A tape arrives showing Fred standing over Renee's dismembered body.
Fred is convicted of her murder and put on death row.
Blinding headaches take hold in the cell, and one morning Fred is gone and a young mechanic named Pete Dayton is in his place.
Baffled police release Pete to his parents, who will not say what they saw the night he appeared.
Pete goes back to work at the garage, where the gangster Mr. Eddy is a favoured customer.
Mr. Eddy brings his girlfriend Alice Wakefield, Renee's double as a blonde, to the garage, and she and Pete begin an affair.
Alice tells Pete that Mr. Eddy - the pornographer Dick Laurent - forced her into his films at gunpoint.
Mr. Eddy telephones Pete and puts the Mystery Man on to explain what happens to men who sleep with his girlfriend.
Alice talks Pete into robbing and killing the fence Andy so the two of them can run.
Pete kills Andy by accident and sees a photograph of Alice and Renee together in Mr. Eddy's world.
Alice and Pete drive to a cabin in the desert and have sex on the sand, and she tells him he will never have her.
Alice walks into the cabin and the man who stands up outside is Fred Madison again.
The Mystery Man films Fred at the cabin and tells him that the woman's name is Renee.
Fred takes Mr. Eddy into the desert, cuts his throat with the Mystery Man's help, and is shown a screen playing his own life back at him.
Fred drives to his own house and speaks into the intercom the words the film opened with: "Dick Laurent is dead."
Police give chase down the highway as Fred's face distorts and the film ends where it began.
syuzhet_notes: The film is a closed loop: told-order bullet 1 is Fred hearing through his own intercom the message that told-order bullet 18 shows him delivering, so the first scene of the film is caused by its second-to-last. Apart from that closure the telling runs forward, but it runs forward through a transformation that swaps one protagonist for another at told-order bullet 7 and swaps back at bullet 16, leaving the two halves impossible to lay on one timeline with any confidence.
fabula_notes: The film offers no account of Fred's transformation into Pete, so this chronology treats it as literal succession, which is one reading among several; the common alternative is that the Pete material is a fugue Fred constructs on death row, in which case bullets 7-15 are not later than bullets 5-6 but simultaneous with them. Whether Renee and Alice are the same woman is deliberately unresolved.
